EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Luhao Zhao
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: Good morning everyone, today I'm starting to design the high-level information architecture for the system. I'll be basing it on the user personas and the initial PRD draft completed in the previous project. @Yu Su @Peng Hou Regarding the information architecture, I'd like to confirm first: should we prioritize organizing information from the perspective of user roles (executives, finance, sustainability department), or from the perspective of business processes (data entry, accounting, reporting)? Or a combination of both?

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Yu Su
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: @Luhao Zhao Good question. Personally, I suggest combining both approaches in the initial stage. First, use the core business process (data collection -> accounting analysis -> asset management -> report output) as the main thread. Then, within each stage, organize the presentation of information based on the concerns of different user roles. For example, in the executive view, highlight strategic KPIs and charts.

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Luhao Zhao
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: @Yu Su Understood, this idea is very clear. Then I will first draw the first draft of the information architecture based on the principle of "process-centric, role-assisted".

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Luhao Zhao
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: Everyone, I'd like to sync up on the progress of the information architecture design. Based on the "process-centric, role-supplementary" principle discussed with Yu Su last week, I have already drafted a high-level information architecture. It mainly revolves around four major modules: "Data Ingestion - Accounting Management - Asset Management - Reporting and Analysis," and I've planned corresponding view entry points for different roles. The Figma link has been sent to the group. Product and design colleagues, please take a look and provide your feedback. @Yu Su @Peng Hou @Jingwei Sun

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Yu Su
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: @Luhao Zhao Received. This structure is very clear, and the main process is clear at a glance. This afternoon, I will carefully check whether the sub-function division under each module is reasonable, especially the related parts of asset management and accounting rules.

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Lizhen Zhou
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: @Luhao Zhao Just looked at the information architecture draft, it's very good. Please make sure that the "Carbon Asset Management" module can clearly map the accounting subjects and cost allocation logic that the finance department cares about, which is crucial for subsequent compliance audits.

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Luhao Zhao
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: @Lizhen Zhou Received, Boss Zhou. I will focus on refining the structure of this part in the next iteration and confirm with you again.

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Luhao Zhao
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: @Lizhen Zhou @Yu Su Good afternoon, regarding the system's high-level information architecture, I have deepened the relevant modules based on Boss Zhou's suggestion yesterday that "carbon asset management needs to be mapped to accounting subjects." I have re-sort out (re-organized/re-evaluated) the entire information flow of "carbon assets" from recognition, measurement to reporting, and tried to reflect the connection with the financial cost center and accounting subjects in the architecture. The new draft has been updated, please help me check again if it is closer to the needs of financial auditing.

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Lizhen Zhou
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: @Luhao Zhao, thank you for your hard work. I've seen it, and this direction is correct. It's very important to bring financial logic forward into information architecture design. I suggest we have a 15-minute quick meeting with @Yu Su, and I'll give you a specific cost allocation example so you can have a better feel for the design.

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Yu Su
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: Good suggestion! @Luhao Zhao, Boss Zhou and I are available anytime. Once we fully grasp this core logic, our subsequent product feature definitions will be very clear. This is one of our core competitive advantages.

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Luhao Zhao
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: Great! Thanks, Boss Zhou and Yu Su! Then I'll send a meeting invitation right away, how about now?

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Luhao Zhao
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: @Lizhen Zhou @Yu Su Good afternoon, thank you very much for yesterday afternoon's meeting. Boss Zhou's sharing of cost allocation cases gave me a deeper understanding of the financial logic of carbon asset management. I have integrated these logics into the high-level information architecture diagram, especially in the "Carbon Asset Management" module, detailing the information flow path from asset recognition, measurement, amortization to retirement. The new draft has been updated to Figma, please help review it again to see if it accurately reflects the financial needs.

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Lizhen Zhou
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: @Luhao Zhao So efficient! I just saw the new architecture diagram, and it's much clearer this time! It shows the mapping of accounting subjects and the association of cost centers, which ensures that subsequent product functions will not deviate from financial compliance from an information architecture perspective. Very good, I have no more questions.

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Yu Su
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: @Luhao Zhao This architecture really captures the essence. From a product perspective, this information architecture provides a solid foundation for us to define specific functions like carbon asset accounting and impairment testing later on. Great work!

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Luhao Zhao
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: @all Here's an update. Yesterday afternoon, the high-level information architecture diagram received positive feedback from Boss Lizhen Zhou and Yu Su. The logic regarding the association between carbon assets, financial cost centers, and accounting subjects in the diagram was recognized by both business and finance. I have uploaded the updated draft to Confluence as the basis for our subsequent discussions. It is expected to be finalized and archived tomorrow.

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Lizhen Zhou
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: @Luhao Zhao Thank you for your hard work. This architectural design is very solid and lays a firm foundation for subsequent financial compliance functions.

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Yu Su
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: Well done! @Luhao Zhao With this clear information architecture, our product team can more confidently break down and design subsequent user stories and features.

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Luhao Zhao
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: Good morning everyone! Here's some good news: The final version of the task [Design System High-Level Information Architecture] has been completed, incorporating the valuable feedback from Boss Lizhen Zhou and Yu Su. The diagram clearly reflects the logical connection between carbon assets and financial cost centers. I have archived the final version in Confluence, and this task is officially complete! Thank you all for your support!

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Lizhen Zhou
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: @Luhao Zhao, great work! This information architecture provides a clear blueprint for our subsequent financial compliance function design, which is very valuable. Congratulations on the successful completion of the task!

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Yu Su
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: @Luhao Zhao, excellent work! With this solid architecture, we'll have much more confidence in breaking down our subsequent product features. Congratulations!

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Lujian Gao
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: Hello everyone, today I'm starting a new design task: [Designing a File Storage Solution]. Considering that our system will need to store a large number of supporting documents, reports, etc. in the future, I will focus on comparing Azure Blob and AWS S3. The evaluation dimensions will include cost, API ease of use, access permission management, and the difficulty of integration with our existing technology stack. A preliminary selection recommendation report will be provided early next week.

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Lujian Gao
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: Good morning everyone. Regarding the design of our file storage solution, I conducted a preliminary evaluation of Azure Blob and AWS S3 last Friday. From the perspective of cost and ecosystem integration, AWS S3 has a slight advantage, and our other projects are also on AWS. Today, I will start designing the Bucket Policy and directory structure based on S3, for example, isolating by tenant and file type.

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Lujian Gao
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: I'm updating you on the progress of the file storage solution. The technical selection has been finalized as AWS S3. Today, I am designing the Bucket Policy to ensure that sensitive files (such as audit reports, certification documents) uploaded by different enterprise tenants are physically isolated and invisible to each other. I am also planning the lifecycle policy to automatically transfer archived files older than one year to a lower-cost storage tier.

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Lujian Gao
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: Morning. I've completed the draft design for our file storage solution (AWS S3), specifically regarding bucket permission policies and lifecycle rules, ensuring data isolation between different tenants. Today, I'm mainly working on writing the accompanying documentation, explaining our recommended directory structure, such as how to organize voucher files from different vendors and years. I expect to have the complete solution ready by tomorrow.

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Weihua Zhang
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: Today, several key design tasks were completed on time, which is great. Hao Zhao's user journey map pointed us in the right direction, and the architecture designs by Hao Zhao (another project) and Lujian Gao also paved the way for subsequent development. Everyone, let's keep up this pace.

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Lujian Gao
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: Good morning everyone, regarding the file storage solution, the complete technical design document (based on AWS S3) has been uploaded to Confluence. It includes three main parts: bucket permission policies, lifecycle rules, and recommended directory structure. @Mingzhi Li Boss Li, please review it.

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Mingzhi Li
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: @Lujian Gao I've finished reviewing the document on the file storage solution. The design is very comprehensive, especially the considerations for tenant data isolation and cost optimization. The proposal is approved and can be finalized.

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Lujian Gao
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: Received, Boss Li. I will formally close the task for [Design File Storage Solution]. The final version of the document has been marked as final in Confluence.

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Yang Zhao
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: No problem, Boss Chen. I'll check immediately. Also, I'm officially starting today to create high-fidelity UI design mockups for the login, registration, and forgot password pages. I will design based on the existing wireframes and PRD. @Guohua Yin, regarding the "forgot password" process, are there any particular security or usability details I need to pay attention to?

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Guohua Yin
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: @Yang Zhao Good question. Regarding the "forgot password" process, our main security consideration is to prevent "user enumeration attacks." Therefore, regardless of whether the email entered by the user exists or not, the feedback message should be consistent, such as "If this email address is registered, you will receive an email containing a password reset link," instead of directly prompting "user does not exist." Please ensure the UI copy adheres to this principle.

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Yang Zhao
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: Received, thanks for the reminder. I will clarify this in the design draft and interaction specifications. @Huilan Chen Boss Chen, I just did a final check on the optimized design draft. All components and styles are highly consistent with the design system, and the overall visual effect is great! Especially the changes to the supplier submission process, the experience is much smoother. No problem!

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Yang Zhao
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: Morning~ I have two tasks today. One is to continue advancing the high-fidelity design of the login/registration page. I will implement the interactive copy for the "forgot password" flow to prevent user enumeration attacks, as mentioned by Guohua Yin last week. The other is to start the high-fidelity design of the new supplier admission process page. I will first study the relevant PRD and flowcharts before starting the design.

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Yang Zhao
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: Here's an update on today's design progress: The high-fidelity UI mockups for the login/registration page have been completed according to the security prompts, and the Figma link has been updated. @Huilan Chen Boss Chen @Guohua Yin, please take a look when you have a moment. The draft for the supplier access process is also almost done, and I'll continue to refine it tomorrow.

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Mingzhi Li
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: Good morning everyone, today we have a few new tasks starting and a few ongoing ones. Let's all synchronize our plans.

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Yang Zhao
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: Morning! My tasks are quite concentrated today. First, I'll continue to advance the high-fidelity mockups for the login/registration and supplier access processes, especially the 'forgot password' flow. I'll strictly follow the security principles mentioned by Guohua Yin last week to ensure that the prompt text doesn't expose user information. Second, today I'll start the high-fidelity design for the data entry form page. This page has complex interactions, so I'll first lay out a framework.

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Yang Zhao
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: Here's a quick update on today's work: The high-fidelity design for the login/registration/forgot password pages is mostly complete, and the Figma link has been updated. About 70% of the UI for the supplier access process is also done. The page framework and core interactive prototype for the data entry form have also been set up, and I'll continue to refine the visual design tomorrow. @Huilan Chen, Boss Chen, you can take a look at the prototype when you have a moment.

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Huilan Chen
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: Good morning everyone, a new day has begun. @Yang Zhao, Boss Li also mentioned yesterday that you have a heavy workload, so please prioritize carefully. What are the progress plans for the landing page, supplier access, and data entry today? Specifically, can the interactive prototype for data entry be ready today? @Xinjie Li @Yutong Song @Zixuan Qin, please also share your respective plans.

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: Good morning, Boss Chen! Received. I will prioritize finishing the login/registration page today, ensuring all interaction details comply with security standards. For the high-fidelity draft of the supplier access process, I expect to advance it by about 30% today. As for the interactive prototype of the data entry form, I already built the framework yesterday, and today I will connect the core logic for field grouping, real-time validation, and draft saving. I'll send it to you for review this afternoon.

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Mingzhi Li
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: @Yang Zhao The priority arrangement is good, proceed as planned. @Xinjie Li Excellent, containerization is the foundation of deployment automation, get on it. @Yutong Song For Zustand practices, you can document more to facilitate team sharing. @Zixuan Qin The Dashboard is the facade, the information architecture needs to be clear and highlight key points.

EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Huilan Chen
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: Good morning, everyone. EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Yang Zhao
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: Good morning, Boss Chen! Received. The design draft for the login/registration page will definitely be delivered today; I'm currently doing the final detail walkthrough. EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.speaker: Mingzhi Li
EverMemBench-Dynamic@a6b210a32248e841967.dialogue: Everyone's progress is very clear. @Yang Zhao, please finalize the login page today.
